c181.title: On the hospital ward
c181.story: On her first day on the hospital ward, Ira met many patients. A young man was happy because his [[tumor]] was not cancer. A brave girl was fighting [[leukemia]], and an old teacher was weak from [[anemia]]. A boy had a rare [[syndrome]], and a little girl showed Ira her [[asthma]] inhaler. A tourist had [[diarrhea]] after drinking tap water, and a painter had [[vertigo]]. At lunch, an old doctor told her stories about [[polio]] and the first [[penicillin]]. Once, he said, a quick [[antidote]] saved a farmer after a snake bite. In one study, some patients felt better after taking only a [[placebo]]. Long ago, [[cholera]] spread through the dirty water of the city. In the evening, Ira helped a family find a quiet [[hospice]] for their grandfather. She went home tired but proud of her work.

c182.title: A castle in England
c182.story: Anna visited an old castle in England with Max during the summer holidays. They climbed the stone [[bastion]] and looked at the green fields below. A friendly guide said that a rich [[lord]] built the castle long ago. Later, a [[duke]] lived here, and then an [[earl]] bought it. A [[squire]] owned the village nearby, and each [[yeoman]] farmed his own land. The local [[gentry]] came to big dinners in the great hall. Every [[aristocrat]] wore expensive clothes and danced all night. Once, a [[monarch]] visited the castle and sat on a golden [[throne]]. His [[consort]] stood beside him and smiled at the guests. Their son was too young to rule, so his uncle became [[regent]]. A loyal [[vassal]] promised to protect the boy with his life. At the end, Anna posed like a queen for Max's camera.

c183.title: Empires of the East
c183.story: On Tuesday, Taras had a history lesson about great empires of the East. First, the teacher showed a picture of a [[sultan]] in his huge palace. The women of his family lived in a separate part called the [[harem]]. A loyal [[eunuch]] guarded its doors day and night. Next, the class read about a wise [[caliph]] who loved books and science. His [[caliphate]] was bigger than many countries today. Then came a powerful [[khan]] and his army of horse riders. His people were [[nomads|nomad]] who moved their tents across the wide [[steppe]]. Taras laughed at a drawing of a hairy [[yak]] carrying their bags. Finally, a rich [[maharaja]] signed an [[edict]] that opened free schools for poor children. For homework, Taras drew a map of all four empires and got the best mark.

c184.title: Warriors of the past
c184.story: Max loves military history, so he spent all Saturday with a thick book. First, he read about a brave [[gladiator]] who fought in a huge arena. A Roman [[centurion]] led a hundred men from his [[legion]] across the hills. In the next chapter, a [[paladin]] defended a small [[fort]] against a big army. Max loved the part where a [[musketeer]] fought a [[duel]] at dawn. Then he read about a [[samurai]] with two swords who served the [[shogun]]. The last story was about a [[commodore]] at sea. His few small ships faced a huge enemy [[armada]]. With a clever [[maneuver]], he hid his ships behind an island and won. In the evening, Max told Anna every story, and she fell asleep on the sofa.

c185.title: The Wild West
c185.story: On Friday night, Taras watched an old western with his dad. The first [[colonists|colonist]] arrived by ship and built small towns by the sea. Years later, a family of [[pioneers|pioneer]] traveled west to the [[frontier]]. They got fifty [[acres|acre]] of land near a quiet river. An old [[trapper]] lived alone in the forest and sold them furs. In town, a young [[cowboy]] with a [[revolver]] ordered a [[whiskey]] in the [[saloon]]. Suddenly, news came by [[telegraph]]: [[bandits|bandit]] planned to rob the afternoon train. They had [[dynamite]] and wanted to blow up the bridge. The [[sheriff]] took his big [[magnum]] and rode to the bridge with the cowboy. They got there just before the old [[locomotive]] arrived. The bandits ran away, and the train crossed safely. Taras's dad fell asleep before the end, so Taras told him the story at breakfast.

c186.title: Dark times
c186.story: On a rainy Sunday, Anna and Max visited a history museum in Kyiv. The first hall showed portraits of the last [[tsar]] and the German [[kaiser]]. A guide explained how [[imperialism]] made old empires hungry for more land. After the First World War, [[fascism]] grew in several countries in Europe. Old posters showed [[fascists|fascist]] marching in long, straight lines. In Germany, the [[national socialists|national socialist]] made the [[swastika]] their symbol. The quietest room told the story of the [[Holocaust|holocaust]], and many visitors cried there. The guide said that every [[genocide]] starts with hate and silence. In another hall, a [[dictator]] smiled from a poster full of [[propaganda]]. Next to it were letters from a brave [[dissident]] who spent years in prison. The last room showed how people stopped a military [[junta]] with peaceful protests. Outside, Anna held Max's hand and said, "We must remember all of this."

c187.title: Easter with Grandma
c187.story: At Easter, Anna went to church with Grandma early in the morning. The [[pastor]] spoke about the [[archangel]] Michael and the coming of the [[messiah]]. After the service, they had tea with Grandma's friend Rosa, a [[Catholic]] from Lviv. Rosa explained that in [[Catholicism]], baptism and marriage are each a [[sacrament]]. She showed them a small [[crucifix]] from her mother. She also explained which old books are part of the Bible's [[canon]]. Her cousin once saw a [[cardinal]] in a red robe at a [[synod]] in Rome. Grandma remembered her own father, who met a kind [[padre]] in the army. The man prayed with the soldiers before every hard day. Later, Rosa invited them to a monastery where an old [[abbot]] makes honey. Anna said yes at once, because she loves honey more than anything.

c188.title: An evening of many faiths
c188.story: Anna's college held an evening of many faiths in the big hall. First, a [[Protestant]] student talked about her church choir. A [[Baptist]] from a small town shared his family's Sunday traditions. A friendly [[Mormon]] spoke about helping neighbors, and an old [[Quaker|quaker]] talked about silence and peace. Then a Jewish [[cantor]] sang a beautiful old song. Next, an [[imam]] and another [[cleric]] explained the basics of [[Islam]]. They told the students about fasting during [[Ramadan]] and sharing food with the poor. Pork and alcohol, they said, are [[haram]] for many Muslims. The imam explained that [[jihad]] means struggle, often to be a better person. He added that an [[Islamist]] has political goals, which is different from simply being Muslim. At the end, everyone ate cookies together, and Max ate the most.

c189.title: A yoga retreat
c189.story: Anna's friend Lisa went on a yoga [[retreat]] in the mountains for a week. On the first day, a calm [[swami]] taught the group to breathe slowly. A [[brahmin]] from the village told them about the heart [[chakra]]. He also explained [[karma]] and [[dharma]], the idea of duty and right living. Every morning they repeated a [[mantra]], and one man even fell into a [[trance]]. On Wednesday, a [[Buddhist]] teacher came with an old [[lama]]. The old man talked about [[Buddhism]] and read a [[sutra]] in a soft voice. Lisa's favorite [[ritual]] was green tea at sunset with the group. A quiet woman with an [[aura]] of calm became her friend. She taught Lisa about the [[Tao]] and the calm force of [[yin]]. On the last day, Lisa asked her teacher how to reach [[nirvana]]. He smiled and said, "Start by turning off your phone."

c190.title: Heaven, hell and spirits
c190.story: After a horror film, Max and Anna argued all the way home. Max is an [[atheist]], and his [[atheism]] makes horror films funny for him. Anna asked him if he believed in [[paradise]] or [[demons|demon]]. "In the film, the [[antichrist]] was just a scary little boy," Max laughed. Anna said the [[exorcism]] scene was the worst part. Max said the [[exorcist]] looked like their math teacher. Then they argued about whether [[armageddon]] would ever come. Max said he does not like any [[dogma]], old or new. Anna called him a little [[inquisitor]] because he asked so many questions. At home, they read about [[voodoo]] and a [[jinn]] in a lamp. Anna's mom, a true [[skeptic]], said, "No more scary stories tonight, please." Then she quietly checked under her own bed.

c191.title: Grandma's folk tales
c191.story: On a snowy evening, Grandma told Anna and Max old tales from world [[folklore]]. First came a hungry [[ghoul]] who lived in an old cemetery. Then a [[banshee]] cried in the night, and a tiny [[leprechaun]] hid his gold. Max liked the story of a [[yeti]] who helped lost climbers in the mountains. Anna loved the [[phoenix]] that rose again from its own ashes. Next, Grandma told them about a village [[healer]] who gave a sick boy a [[talisman]]. A [[druid]] in the forest made a magic [[elixir]] from herbs. Far away, a [[shaman]] danced around a tall [[totem]] to call the rain. The people of one tribe prayed to a golden [[idol]] in a cave. A [[charlatan]] tried to sell the villagers fake magic, but nobody bought it. "And where did your old ring come from?" Max asked Grandma. Grandma just smiled, and the ring stayed an [[enigma]].

c192.title: Hey, mhm, pardon?
c192.story:
Anna: [[Hey|hey]], Max!
Max: [[Yo|yo]], Anna! What's up?
Anna: Let's go to the cinema tonight.
Max: [[Mhm|mhm]]. Which film?
Anna: [[Hmm|hmm]], maybe the funny one.
Max: [[Pardon|pardon]]? The line is bad.
Anna: The funny film! At six.
Max: [[Okey-dokey|okey-dokey]]. See you at six.
Anna: [[Bye|bye]]!
